prerequisites: elementary functions including trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions

learning_outcomes.text: Understand, describe and solve simple problems of mathematical analysis for one-real-variable functions.

Acquire knowledge and understanding of the basic notions of the analysis of one variable functions, computation of limits, derivatives and integrals, qualitative study of functions, study of sequences and series of real numbers.
Ability to tackle problems with logical accuracy and find the most suitable techniques for solving them.
Frame problems (even new problems) in the most suitable framework, identify the characteristic features of problems and the connections with theoretical results.
Articulate a given topic in a consistent way arguing with a precise mathematical language.
Develop a methodological approach to improve learning capabilities.

syllabus_topics: Real Numbers: order relation, infimum and supremum, maximum and minimum, topology
Sequences and series of real numbers
One variable functions: fundamental functions; monotone functions; composite and inverse functions; limit, continuity, derivative and tangent line, higher order derivatives, convexity and concavity
Integral Calculus of one variable functions: definite and indefinite integral, fundamental theorem of calculus, integration methods; improper integrals
assessment_rules: The final exam is split into a written and an oral exam. Only after passing the written exam with a minimum score of 18/30 can the student access the oral exam. The final grade corresponds to the arithmetic mean of the grades obtained in the written and oral exams. Students pass if they demonstrate knowledge of key concepts and correct use of mathematical language.
bibliography: M. Bertsch, R. Dal Passo, L. Giacomelli, "Analisi Matematica", Seconda edizione, McGraw-Hill.
M. Bramanti. Esercitazioni di Analisi Matematica 1. Esculapio.
